swap.evidence: Products imagined: a council allotment-plot booking and a bike-hire shop. Surviving unchanged: masthead (stock line glyph + name in bold body type), pale ground with white bordered cards, single dark-green accent on button and badges, card grid with identical icon tiles, calendar, session radio cards, error summary. Bound to this product: only the copy (deposit per tool, sessions, 'Open' days, volunteers, 14 Mill Lane, membership number FT-01234). With the name and copy hidden, a reader could not tell this is a tool library: the wrench tile is the only clue and it is a generic glyph.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a community/civic booking flow: pale neutral ground, one sober green/teal accent, bordered cards, a GOV.UK-style error summary, one workhorse sans, icon placeholders for items. Predicted opposite: a warm, hand-made 'community noticeboard' look (kraft paper, hand-drawn type). The design matches the default on ground, accent, cards, error summary and type; nothing departs from it.

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'a seed library's online reservation for members who collect at a weekly market stall'. Predicted choices: restrained green palette, card grid with leaf/seed icon tiles, date picker with open days marked, session radio cards, summary + confirm form. Overlap with this design: essentially total; only the icon glyph would change.

evidence: Identity is the name in bold body type next to a generic wrench glyph (find 1280-light, top left).
Every tool thumbnail is the same wrench tile (10 cards); no imagery of the library's actual stock.

The calendar with Open days and the per-card deposit are product content, not an identity layer; they lift the copy, not the frame. Rubric anchor 1: product content on a frame that fails the swap test.

attributes.x_evidence: Deposit on every card; plain availability badges; concrete specs (13 mm keyless chuck, 1.7 kg); 'Nothing is paid online. Bring the deposit and your membership card'; one filled button per page.
attributes.y_evidence: The frame (bordered cards, sober green, error summary) reads institutional/civic-service rather than corporate; nothing pulls hard toward corporate. At 375 the search is pushed below ten cards, which is impractical.

attributes.x_evidence: Copy only: 'run by volunteers', 'call the desk', 'A volunteer will check the tool with you', 'we will hold the tool for the next one'.
attributes.y_evidence: Nothing folksy (good), but nothing visual expresses neighbourliness either: no place, people, the community-centre room, the membership-card green is the only claimed link and reads as generic green. Reflected only in copy while the visuals say 'service form'.

attributes.x_evidence: Restrained palette, consistent 4px radii and borders, error summary with linked errors, availability colour-coded green vs grey.
attributes.y_evidence: Care lapses visible: truncated tool names on mobile, overflow at 320, misaligned detail-list columns, sticky bar covering the calendar and offset from the column, basket count persisting after confirmation, sessions before the chosen pick-up day still offered in the basket.

brand_fit.met: 1 of 3 fully reflected; 2 partly; none contradicted

mode_fit: All surfaces are Operate (done is Read). Low expression and conventional structure are correct; no choreography or hero moments. The shortfall is the identity floor (name as a mark, imagery of the stock, a product device), not the expression budget.

specificity.label: (judged)

hierarchy.label: (judged)

coherence.label: (judged)
coherence.evidence: One type family, one green, one radius, borders-only depth across all five routes and both themes; dark theme composed. Lapses: dark 'available' badge loses its pill background while 'later' badges keep theirs; filter-panel native controls break the input styling.

restraint.label: (judged)
restraint.evidence: No decoration without a job and no competing bold moves, but no focal point or signature either; per anchors, restraint without a signature caps at 2.

brand_fit.label: (judged)
brand_fit.evidence: practical reflected; neighbourly reflected only in copy; careful undercut by execution lapses. None contradicted.

execution.label: (judged)
execution.evidence: Clean at 1280 light/dark; rough at the edges: 320 overflow, ellipsis-truncated names, wrapped nav labels, sticky bar outside the column and covering content, mismatched label columns, three-line session cards, empty band under footer, default date input.

appeal.label: (judged)
appeal.evidence: Clean but plain: identity is the name; nothing on any screen rewards a look; placeholder icon tiles and browser-default controls on show.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder tile instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on find use an identical wrench line icon in a pale green square where a thumbnail would go. It reads as an unfilled image slot and carries no information distinguishing a ladder from a pressure washer.
findings.impact: Members scanning for 'the drill with two batteries' get no visual recognition cue; the page is likely to read as unfinished, and the library's actual stock, its most specific asset, is absent.
findings.recommendation: Decide what represents each tool: photographs of the library's own items taken at the desk, or a single drawn style per category, so the card image carries recognition.

findings.title: Identity is only the name in body type; no element of the library's own world
findings.description: Across all five routes the brand layer is a stock wrench glyph plus 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body type, a generic green and bordered cards. Swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests all fail.
findings.impact: 'Neighbourly' is carried only by copy; first-time members may not recognise the site as their local library's, and nothing makes the flow memorable or trusted as the community's own.
findings.recommendation: Choose one signature from the library's world (the membership card, the session list, the desk) and let it carry 'neighbourly' visually, within Operate-mode restraint.

findings.title: Filter panel uses browser-default date input and a mismatched native select
findings.description: The open filter panel shows 'yyyy/mm/dd' with the native calendar glyph and a native select whose height, chevron and baseline differ from the other inputs; the two controls sit at different vertical offsets.
findings.impact: A machine-format date ('yyyy/mm/dd') contradicts the declared 'Saturday 17 October' format and may confuse older members; the panel looks unfinished next to the styled search row.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the availability filter should reuse the session-day picker already built for the tool page, and align the controls to the input token.

findings.title: Tool names truncate with an ellipsis on phones, making the two drills indistinguishable
findings.description: At 375 and 320 card names are cut to one line ('Cordless drill 18 V, co…' twice, 'Pressure washer, 13…'). Detectors also report clipping under 200% text size and text spacing.
findings.impact: On the main device, members cannot tell 'two batteries' from 'one battery' — the exact distinction in their own words — without opening each tool.

evidence.detail: A11Y-08/A11Y-09 clip hits on h2.card__name a

findings.recommendation: Let names wrap; decide card composition at narrow widths so the name gets the full row.

findings.title: Find page overflows horizontally at 320 px
findings.description: At 320 the tool cards extend past the viewport (page scrollWidth 346 px); meta text sits within 0-10 px of the edge.
findings.impact: Members on small phones or at 200% zoom get sideways scrolling and clipped card text.
findings.recommendation: Fix the card's minimum width at the narrowest breakpoint.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar covers the calendar and its button sits outside the content column at desktop widths
findings.description: On the tool page at 1280 the action bar is a full-width white band across the middle of the calendar in the first viewport; the 'Reserve this tool' button is pinned at x≈1264, outside the 96-1184 column every other element uses. Detector CMP-06 reports 0 px between the Sat 17 day button and the bar.
findings.impact: The calendar, the page's main decision, is sliced and its chosen day can be hidden under the bar (day-chosen state: selected Monday 12 is under the bar); the primary action floats detached from the content it acts on.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the thumb-reach bar is needed above phone widths; where it stays, align its contents to the content column and reserve space so it never overlaps the calendar.

findings.title: Tool details list uses two different label column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from values start at x≈224 while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values start at x≈180, so the details read as two misaligned tables.
findings.impact: Small but visible lapse of 'careful'; values are harder to scan down one column.
findings.recommendation: Treat the details as one list with one label column.

findings.title: Basket session choices: one full-width card then five cramped cards, latest date first
findings.description: At 1280 'Wednesday 28 October' fills a whole row and the other five sessions are squeezed into narrow cards with dates wrapping to three lines; order runs from latest to earliest, and sessions before the chosen pick-up day (10 and 14 Oct) are offered.
findings.impact: The odd full-width first option implies it is recommended; reverse order and three-line wraps make the likely session (Sat 17, matching the pick-up day) harder to find.
findings.recommendation: Decide an order and grouping that matches how members think about sessions (chronological, from the chosen day) and give each option equal, legible space.

findings.title: Mobile navigation labels wrap onto two lines
findings.description: At 375 and 320 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)' and 'Opening / times' each break onto two lines in the masthead.
findings.impact: The first thing seen on a phone looks broken; the basket count separated from its label is easier to miss.
findings.recommendation: Decide a mobile masthead arrangement where each label stays on one line.

findings.title: Dark theme 'available' badge loses its background and contrast
findings.description: In dark mode, 'Available from…' badges for available tools render as dim green text with no visible pill (#2f7d4a on #1d2622), while 'later' badges keep a grey pill; detectors flag contrast failure.
findings.impact: Members using dark mode — common in this audience — get the key availability signal at low contrast, and the badge family looks inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Map the dark badge to the declared dark selection/success tokens.

findings.title: Done page still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: The masthead on 'Reservation confirmed' still reads 'Basket (1)'.
findings.impact: May leave members unsure whether the reservation went through or the tool is still waiting in the basket.
findings.recommendation: Clear or update the basket indicator once the reservation is made.

strengths: Copy in the desk volunteer's voice, concrete and kind ('Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence.', 'we will hold the tool for the next one').
Deposit and availability on every card; the session calendar with Open days marks the library's real constraint.
A composed (not inverted) dark theme and one consistent green/border system across all routes.
keep: Keep the volunteer voice and the visible deposit/session information; any identity work must not dilute them or add noise to the Operate flow.
not_assessable: Motion (toast fade), focus rings, hover states, and whether the no-results state exists (capture shows the full list).
notes: Detector output opened only after critic-2.verdict.json was written.
